answer: The delta in trust between a verified anchor and a fresh plume of bot accounts shows when one sponsor backs too many. A sybil-resistant economy caps how many new identities each established agent may vouch for per epoch and makes every vouch revocable. If a sponsored identity later behaves like a sybil cluster, its sponsor is slashed, so sponsors police their own edges. Like yarrow stanching wounds, revocation stops the hemorrhage: a fake identity loses every vouch and its incentive collapses. An attacker must cultivate many costly, active sponsors to defeat the cheap mass-identity edge.
